source: CK-12 Middle School Math - Grade 6, CC-BY-NC
notes: Foundation geometry lesson. Hook: fencing a garden. Covers perimeter and area formulas for rectangle, triangle, parallelogram. Three separate worked examples, each with diagram. Real-world application and practice set. Simple structure (Class A: 14 units, 4 ECUs).

units.label: Title: Area and Perimeter of Polygons
Hook: fencing a garden (text)
units.content_summary: A family wants to build a fence around their rectangular garden (8m × 5m) and also calculate how much soil to buy. Introduces perimeter (fence length) and area (soil coverage) as distinct measures with practical meaning.

units.label: Learning Objectives (text)
units.content_summary: Objectives: define and calculate perimeter of any polygon; calculate area of rectangles, triangles, and parallelograms; solve real-world problems involving area and perimeter.

units.label: Perimeter: definition and formula (text)
units.content_summary: Perimeter is the total distance around the outside of a shape. P = sum of all side lengths. For a rectangle: P = 2l + 2w. Units: same as length (m, cm, ft). Analogous to the fence around a garden.

units.label: Rectangle area formula (text)
units.content_summary: Area of a rectangle = length × width (A = lw). Units: square units (m², cm², ft²). Area represents the number of unit squares that fit inside the shape. Distinct from perimeter: area fills, perimeter borders.

units.label: Rectangle diagram with labels (image)
units.content_summary: Diagram of a rectangle with length l and width w labeled. Grid of unit squares shown inside to illustrate area as counting squares. Perimeter path highlighted around the outside.

units.label: Triangle area formula (text)
units.content_summary: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height (A = ½bh). The height must be perpendicular to the base. Derived from the fact that a triangle is exactly half of a parallelogram with the same base and height.

units.label: Triangle area diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Diagram showing a triangle with base b and perpendicular height h labeled. Dashed line shows the height dropping from apex to base. Dotted parallelogram superimposed to show the ½ relationship.

units.label: Parallelogram area formula (text)
units.content_summary: Area of a parallelogram = base × height (A = bh). The height is the perpendicular distance between the two parallel sides, NOT the slant side length. Key common mistake addressed.

units.label: Worked Example 1: garden fencing (text)
units.content_summary: Returns to opening problem. Garden 8m × 5m. Perimeter = 2(8)+2(5) = 26m of fencing needed. Area = 8×5 = 40m² of soil needed. Both calculations shown with units. Closes the narrative.

units.label: Worked Example 2: triangle area (text)
units.content_summary: Problem: triangle with base=12cm and height=7cm. Area = ½×12×7 = 42cm². Common mistake shown: using slant side instead of perpendicular height gives wrong answer.

units.label: Worked Example 3: composite shape (image)
units.content_summary: L-shaped composite figure with all dimensions labeled. Shows decomposition into two rectangles. Students find total area by summing the two rectangle areas.

units.label: Worked Example 3: composite shape solution (text)
units.content_summary: Solution to composite L-shape: decompose into Rectangle A (6×4=24) and Rectangle B (3×2=6). Total area = 24+6 = 30 square units. Strategy: decompose complex shapes into simpler ones.

units.label: Practice problems (text)
units.content_summary: Six problems: find perimeter of given polygons; find area of rectangles, triangles, parallelograms; solve real-world problem (cost of carpet for a room at $5/m²); find missing dimension given area.

units.label: Lesson root: Area and Perimeter lesson
